No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

Most scripts used in India today descend from Brāhmī, the script of most of Aśoka's edicts. The lecture traces that family, reads a line of an edict with the audience, and shows how epigraphists date an inscription from the shapes of its letters.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • Brāhmī, the script of most of Aśoka's edicts
  • How Brāhmī grew into the scripts of north and south India
  • A line of an edict, read together
  • Dating an inscription from the shape of its letters

How the time is spent

  1. Scripts and languages 20 min

    Separate writing systems from spoken languages.

    You: pair exercises

  2. Brahmi history 45 min

    Read letter form examples.

    You: symbol tracing

  3. Regional development 25 min

    Sharada and other branches using dated inscriptions.

    You: chronology map

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Distinguish a writing system from the spoken language it is used to write.
  • Trace how Brāhmī developed into the scripts of north and south India.
  • Recognise how epigraphists date an inscription from the shapes of its letters.
